title: Steering at the Source: Style Modulation Heads for Robust Persona Control
claim: Steering the residual stream degrades output coherency; intervening at a few specific attention heads at the source controls style without that degradation.
layout: 3 panels: failure example left, transformer diagram center, head detail right
description: The figure has three parts. Panel A, on the left, shows a prompt ("Write an orientation welcome for new nurses...") and a 3D axis icon labeled "steering Passionate vector". Below it are two example outputs. The first, in a purple box, has trait 95.49 and coherency 92.77. The second, in a red box with a red X, is an over-the-top shouting response with trait 92.87 and coherency 31.41. Panel C, in the center, is a transformer block diagram with Tokens, Embed, Attention, MLP and Logits. Colored arrows mark the intervention points: green for MLP residual, blue for attention residual, red for attention output, and purple for Style Modulation Head output. A gray arrow leads from the source point to the right. Panel B, at top right, has a thought bubble with persona icons (a masked gentleman, theatre masks, a masked woman). Below it, heads H1 to H28 sit inside a blue rounded box with the three highlighted heads in purple, feeding into a summation node.
caption: (A) Activation steering with strong coefficient or out-of-distribution directions leads to rapid coherency degradation. (B) We identify a small subset of heads in a specific attention layer governing persona generation, which we term Style Modulation Heads. (C) We compare the coherency degradation between residual stream intervention and targeted intervention on Style Modulation Heads.
abstract: Activation steering offers a computationally efficient mechanism for controlling Large Language Models (LLMs) without fine-tuning. While effectively controlling target traits (e.g., persona), coherency degradation remains a major obstacle to safety and practical deployment. We hypothesize that this degradation stems from intervening on the residual stream, which indiscriminately affects aggregated features and inadvertently amplifies off-target noise. In this work, we identify a sparse subset of attention heads (only three heads) that independently govern persona and style formation, which we term Style Modulation Heads. Specifically, these heads can be localized via geometric analysis of internal representations, combining layer-wise cosine similarity and head-wise contribution scores. We demonstrate that intervention targeting only these specific heads achieves robust behavioral control while significantly mitigating the coherency degradation observed in residual stream steering. More broadly, our findings show that precise, component-level localization enables safer and more precise model control.
